verses.zh: 弟兄们，我现在对明白律法的人说，你们岂不晓得律法管人是在活着的时候吗？
verses.en: Or do you not know, brothers and sisters[NOTE:1] (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law is lord over a person[NOTE:2] as long as he lives?
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:13.
Here person refers to a human being.

verses.zh: 就如女人有了丈夫，丈夫还活着，就被律法约束；丈夫若死了，就脱离了丈夫的律法。
verses.en: For a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives, but if her[NOTE:1] husband dies, she is released from the law of the marriage.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “the,” with the article used as a possessive pronoun (ExSyn 215).

Grk “husband.”sn Paul’s example of the married woman and the law of the marriage illustrates that death frees a person from obligation to the law. Thus, in spiritual terms, a person who has died to what controlled us (v. 6) has been released from the law to serve God in the new life produced by the Spirit.

verses.zh: 所以丈夫活着，她若归于别人，便叫淫妇；丈夫若死了，她就脱离了丈夫的律法，虽然归于别人，也不是淫妇。
verses.en: So then,[NOTE:1] if she is joined to another man while her husband is alive, she will be called an adulteress. But if her[NOTE:2] husband dies, she is free from that law, and if she is joined to another man, she is not an adulteress.
notes: There is a double connective here that cannot be easily preserved in English: “consequently therefore,” emphasizing the conclusion of what he has been arguing.
Grk “the,” with the article used as a possessive pronoun (ExSyn 215).

verses.zh: 我的弟兄们，这样说来，你们藉着基督的身体，在律法上也是死了，叫你们归于别人，就是归于那从死里复活的，叫我们结果子给　神。
verses.en: So, my brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] you also died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you could be joined to another, to the one who was raised from the dead, to bear fruit to God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:13.
Grk “that we might bear fruit to God.”

verses.zh: 因为我们属肉体的时候，那因律法而生的恶欲就在我们肢体中发动，以致结成死亡的果子。
verses.en: For when we were in the flesh,[NOTE:1] the sinful desires,[NOTE:2] aroused by the law, were active in the members of our body[NOTE:3] to bear fruit for death.
notes: That is, before we were in Christ.
Or “sinful passions.”
Grk “our members”; the words “of our body” have been supplied to clarify the meaning.

verses.zh: 但我们既然在捆我们的律法上死了，现今就脱离了律法，叫我们服事主，要按着心灵（心灵：或译圣灵）的新样，不按着仪文的旧样。
verses.en: But now we have been released from the law, because we have died[NOTE:1] to what controlled us, so that we may serve in the new life of the Spirit and not under the old written code.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “having died.” The participle ἀποθανόντες (apothanontes) has been translated as a causal adverbial participle.
Grk “in the newness of the Spirit and not in the oldness of the letter.”

verses.zh: 这样，我们可说甚么呢？律法是罪吗？断乎不是！只是非因律法，我就不知何为罪。非律法说「不可起贪心」，我就不知何为贪心。
verses.en: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? Absolutely not! Certainly, I[NOTE:1] would not have known sin except through the law. For indeed I would not have known what it means to desire something belonging to someone else[NOTE:2] if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Romans 7:7-25. There has been an enormous debate over the significance of the first person singular pronouns (“I”) in this passage and how to understand their referent. Did Paul intend (1) a reference to himself and other Christians too; (2) a reference to his own pre-Christian experience as a Jew, struggling with the law and sin (and thus addressing his fellow countrymen as Jews); or (3) a reference to himself as a child of Adam, reflecting the experience of Adam that is shared by both Jews and Gentiles alike (i.e., all people everywhere)? Good arguments can be assembled for each of these views, and each has problems dealing with specific statements in the passage. The classic argument against an autobiographical interpretation was made by W. G. Kümmel, Römer 7 und die Bekehrung des Paulus. A good case for seeing at least an autobiographical element in the chapter has been made by G. Theissen, Psychologische Aspekte paulinischer Theologie [FRLANT], 181-268. One major point that seems to favor some sort of an autobiographical reading of these verses is the lack of any mention of the Holy Spirit for empowerment in the struggle described in Rom 7:7-25. The Spirit is mentioned beginning in 8:1 as the solution to the problem of the struggle with sin (8:4-6, 9).
Grk “I would not have known covetousness.”
A quotation from Exod 20:17 and Deut 5:21.

verses.zh: 然而，罪趁着机会，就藉着诫命叫诸般的贪心在我里头发动；因为没有律法，罪是死的。
verses.en: But sin, seizing the opportunity through the commandment, produced in me all kinds of wrong desires.[NOTE:1] For apart from the law, sin is dead.
notes: Or “covetousness.”

verses.zh: 我以前没有律法是活着的；但是诫命来到，罪又活了，我就死了。
verses.en: And I was once alive apart from the law, but with the coming of the commandment, sin became alive

verses.zh: 那本来叫人活的诫命，反倒叫我死；
verses.en: and I died. So[NOTE:1] I found that the very commandment that was intended to bring life brought death![NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “So” to indicate the result of the statement in the previous verse. Greek style often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” but English style generally does not.
Grk “and there was found in/for me the commandment which was for life—this was for death.”

verses.zh: 因为罪趁着机会，就藉着诫命引诱我，并且杀了我。
verses.en: For sin, seizing the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it I died.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “and through it killed me.”

verses.zh: 这样看来，律法是圣洁的，诫命也是圣洁、公义、良善的。
verses.en: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

verses.zh: 既然如此，那良善的是叫我死吗？断乎不是！叫我死的乃是罪。但罪藉着那良善的叫我死，就显出真是罪，叫罪因着诫命更显出是恶极了。
verses.en: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Absolutely not! But sin, so that it would be shown to be sin, produced death in me through what is good, so that through the commandment sin would become utterly sinful.

gr.gloss: it might be shown to be

verses.zh: 我们原晓得律法是属乎灵的，但我是属乎肉体的，是已经卖给罪了。
verses.en: For we know that the law is spiritual—but I am unspiritual, sold into slavery to sin.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “under sin.”

verses.zh: 因为我所做的，我自己不明白；我所愿意的，我并不做；我所恨恶的，我倒去做。
verses.en: For I don’t understand what I am doing. For I do not do what I want—instead, I do what I hate.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “but what I hate, this I do.”

verses.zh: 若我所做的，是我所不愿意的，我就应承律法是善的。
verses.en: But if I do what I don’t want, I agree that the law is good.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “I agree with the law that it is good.”

verses.zh: 既是这样，就不是我做的，乃是住在我里头的罪做的。
verses.en: But now it is no longer me doing it, but sin that lives in me.

verses.zh: 我也知道，在我里头，就是我肉体之中，没有良善。因为，立志为善由得我，只是行出来由不得我。
verses.en: For I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh. For I want to do the good, but I cannot do it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “For to wish is present in/with me, but not to do it.”

verses.zh: 故此，我所愿意的善，我反不做；我所不愿意的恶，我倒去做。
verses.en: For I do not do the good I want, but I do the very evil I do not want!

verses.zh: 若我去做所不愿意做的，就不是我做的，乃是住在我里头的罪做的。
verses.en: Now if I do what I do not want, it is no longer me doing it but sin that lives in me.

verses.zh: 我觉得有个律，就是我愿意为善的时候，便有恶与我同在。
verses.en: So, I find the law that when I want to do good, evil is present with me.

verses.zh: 因为按着我里面的意思（原文是人），我是喜欢　神的律；
verses.en: For I delight in the law of God in my inner being.

verses.zh: 但我觉得肢体中另有个律和我心中的律交战，把我掳去，叫我附从那肢体中犯罪的律。
verses.en: But I see a different law in my members waging war against the law of my mind and making me captive to the law of sin that is in my members.

verses.zh: 我真是苦啊！谁能救我脱离这取死的身体呢？
verses.en: Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

verses.zh: 感谢　神，靠着我们的主耶稣基督就能脱离了。这样看来，我以内心顺服　神的律，我肉体却顺服罪的律了。
verses.en: Thanks be[NOTE:1] to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then,[NOTE:2] I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but[NOTE:3] with my flesh I serve[NOTE:4] the law of sin.
notes: ‡ Most mss (א* A 1739 1881 M sy) read “I give thanks to God” rather than “Now thanks be to God” (א1 [B] Ψ 33 81 104 365 1506), the reading of NA28. The reading with the verb (εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ, eucharistō tō theō) possibly arose from a transcriptional error in which several letters were doubled (TCGNT 455). The conjunction δέ (de, “now”) is included in some mss as well (א1 Ψ 33 81 104 365 1506), but it should probably not be considered original. The ms support for the omission of δέ is both excellent and widespread (א* A B D 1739 1881 M lat sy), and its addition can be explained as an insertion to smooth out the transition between v. 24 and 25.
There is a double connective here that cannot be easily preserved in English: “consequently therefore,” emphasizing the conclusion of what he has been arguing.
Greek emphasizes the contrast between these two clauses more than can be easily expressed in English.
The words “I serve” have been repeated here for clarity.
